limits: Observer overhead has not been isolated in a controlled console comparison.
Host wall/CPU timings are not GPU execution timestamps.
Signaling thread is not necessarily object owner; only three imported signaling APIs observed.
Registration timing, sampling, bounded overflow, handle/address reuse and partial final windows limit coverage.
Draw means are raw microseconds per sampled draw; extrapolated per-frame totals are approximate.
findings: Almost all sampled waits on the hot event returned success immediately; aggregate wait time cannot be treated as long blocking on that event.
Imported NtSetEvent on thread 6 was observed signaling the event polled by frame-producing thread 8. Higher-level engine purpose is not established.
State/bindings dominate sampled draw preparation: approximately 9.6 ms/frame extrapolated; texture requests and samplers roughly 3-4 ms/frame each.
Source inspection found unconditional invalidation on writes to used float-constant ranges, including identical values; the prevalence and useful savings remain unmeasured.
No material speedup is claimed for this measurement build; 60 FPS remains unachieved.
